question.leadin: Answer some questions about very badly named military operations.
question.text: Operations Breakfast, Lunch, Snack, Dinner, Supper, and Dessert were launched to bomb this country neighboring Vietnam during the Vietnam War.
question.answerHtml: Kingdom of Cambodia [or le Royaume du Cambodge, or Prĕəh Riəciənaacak Kampuciə; accept Democratic Kampuchea or Kâmpŭchéa Prâcheathippadey; accept Srok Khmae]
question.clue: After leading a coup against Norodom Sihanouk, Lon Nol became the President of a certain party in this country, which came to power following Year Zero.

swap.leadin: This woman won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize but could not accept it in person, as the ruling military junta held her under house arrest.
swap.text: Name this activist and politician who became State Counsellor of her country in 2016. Since her rise to power, she has been heavily criticized for her inaction against the persecution of the Rohingya people.
swap.answerHtml: Aung San Suu Kyi ([ong sahn soo chee], but be lenient) (prompt on “Suu” or “Kyi” alone)
swap.clue: She leads the National League for Democracy, which she formed after the 8888 Uprising to protest against General Ne Win's dictatorship.

question.leadin: This man fought his emotions while announcing the failure of a national merger.
question.text: Name this founding father of an Asian city-state that became independent from Malaysia in 1965. This leader passed away in March 2015.
question.clue: This man's government created the Social Development Unit, a state-backed matchmaking agency designed to reverse the effects of his overly-successful "Stop at Two" population control policy.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Southeast Asian independence movements.
swap.text: David Marshall campaigned for the independence of this country. Reforms by its first leader, Lee Kwan Yew, made this city-state one of the four "Asian Tigers" with rapidly-growing economies.
swap.clue: HMS Prince of Wales led a naval group named Force Z assigned to protect this country that was destroyed by Japanese airstrikes prior to an invasion by Tomoyuki Yamashita's forces.

question.leadin: The 30 September Movement was an unsuccessful coup against this leader.
question.text: Name this man who led his country's independence movement along with Mohammad Hatta. This man implemented the doctrine of "Guided Democracy" on his country, until he was forced to step down in 1967.
question.clue: This leader hosted the meeting which led to the formation of the Non-Aligned Movement in his country's city of Bandung.

swap.leadin: Christian de Castries, the losing commander at this battle, was held as a prisoner of war.
swap.text: Name this 1954 battle during which the French got destroyed by the Viet Minh and got kicked straight out of Indochina.
swap.clue: At this battle the defending troops were commanded by Colonel Christian de Castries and it ended the day before the Geneva Accords were signed.

question.text: In 1979, China briefly invaded this southern neighbour, as punishment for its invasion of Cambodia. However, this country is more famously remembered for defeating the US in a bloody war, invoking a famous picture of a helicopter taking off from the American Embassy in Saigon.
question.clue: Mike Gravel read one official government history of this country into the record of the Senate after it was leaked to the press by Daniel Ellsberg.

swap.leadin: This man was captured by General Frederic Funston in the aftermath of the Battle of Tirad Pass.
swap.text: Name this revolutionary leader who was brought back to his country by Admiral George Dewey after the Battle of Manila Bay. This man was the first president of a country that would later gain independence due to the Tydings-McDuffie Act.
swap.clue: His followers killed potential rival General Antonio Luna to insure that he would lead them into such battles as the one at Tirad Pass.

question.leadin: A group of communist rebels in this country formed the Hukbalahap during World War II.
question.text: Name this modern-day country where the Sakdal Uprising and the Moro Crater Massacre took place.
question.clue: One dictator from this country was forced into exile by the People Power Revolution after antagonizing the Moro National Liberation Front, which was later attacked on the order of Joseph Estrada.

swap.leadin: A man named Mongkut spent 25 years as a monk before becoming the king of this country in 1851.
swap.text: Name this country that has been ruled by several kings named Rama from the Chakri Dynasty since the 18th century.
swap.clue: This country was unified under the Thonburi Kingdom after the fall of the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

question.leadin: This alliterative name was adopted by the former Saloth Sar.
question.text: Name this Cambodian fiend who overthrow Lon Nol in 1975 and then killed a million people.
question.clue: This leader, who was referred to as "Brother Number One", helped Prince Sihanouk's ("SEE-uh-nook") attempt to return to power after he was deposed in a coup by Lon Nol.

swap.text: This modern-day country's history saw the Majapahit Empire rise from its incredibly populous island of Java, which is also where this country's Buddhist temple of Borobudur was built.
swap.clue: This modern country's Aceh Sultanate provided 90% of the world's pepper in the late 1800s. The world's biggest Buddhist temple is in this country at Borobudur.

question.leadin: The last site of fighting during this campaign was the city of Hue.
question.text: Name this 1968 wave of attacks that targeted nine cities in all. It included an attack on the U.S. embassy in Saigon by a team of 19 Vietcong guerillas.
question.clue: This event included the Massacre at Hue and a diversionary attack on the combat base of Khe Sanh.

swap.leadin: This country's Kayan people have been nicknamed "giraffe women" for wrapping gold coils around their necks.
swap.text: Name this modern-day country whose Konbaung ("cone-baong") dynasty outlawed the usage of peacock designs on non-royal clothes. This country's traditional longyi waist garment was inspired by Malay sarong.
swap.clue: In the 1400s, an enlightened king of this country used 294 tons of metal to cast a giant bell.

question.leadin: A ruler of this kingdom fell out with his wife Amarindra after she beat one of his concubines with a stick.
question.text: Name this kingdom that signed the Bowring Treaty with Britain. This kingdom's territory was sacked during the Haw Wars.
question.answerHtml: Siam [or Rattanakosin; prompt on Thailand] [the unnamed king is Rama I]
question.clue: A king of this country considerably lessened the trade restrictions of the Burney Treaty by agreeing to the Bowring Treaty with Great Britain.

swap.text: Much earlier, Laos's capital at Vientiane had been sacked by this "great" king of Thailand in 1775. This only member of the Thonburi dynasty defeated the Burmese invaders that had destroyed Ayutthaya and was executed by a general who took the throne as Rama I.
swap.answerHtml: Taksin the Great [or Somdet Phra Chao Taksin Maha Rat]
swap.clue: This ruler stabilized the frontier by conquering the Lanna kingdom after leading a guerilla war to repel an occupation by the Konbaung ("kohn-baong") dynasty of Burma.

question.leadin: A gluttonous ruler of this kingdom sometimes displayed good judgment, like when he bragged about swallowing 300 dishes of curry daily, and sometimes displayed bad judgment, like when he provoked a Mongol invasion.
question.text: Name this first kingdom to unify Burma, which was ruled by Narathihapate (nuh-rah-thee-hah-puh-tay) and was expanded to much of the Irrawaddy valley by Anawrahta (uh-naw-ruh-tah).
question.answerHtml: Pagan (puh-gaan) Kingdom [or Pagan Empire; or Bagan Kingdom; or Bagan Empire]
question.clue: After King Manuha refused to give him a copy of the Triptaka, a king of this empire captured Manuha and 30,000 residents of the Thaton Kingdom in order to relocate them to his capital.

swap.leadin: This uprising peaked after the resignation of Ne Win, Myanmar's socialist dictator for 26 years, who remarked "When the army shoots, it shoots to kill."
swap.text: Name this series of protests in which Ne Win was proven right, as the Tatmadaw cracked down in September, murdered hundreds of demonstrators, and established a new dictatorship under Saw Maung's SLORC.
swap.answerHtml: 8888 Uprising [prompt on People Power Uprising or 1988 Uprising]
swap.clue: This event led to the emergence of a figure who gave a speech called "Freedom From Fear" and founded the National League for Democracy; that figure is Aung San Suu Kyi.

question.text: Along with the islands in the Labuan territory, East Malaysia is made up of these two states found on the north of the island of Borneo.
question.answerHtml: Sabah and Sarawak [order not important but don't accept or prompt on just one]

swap.leadin: In 1857 Chinese laborers revolted against one of these rulers after he instituted a high opium tax, and this dynasty had its capital at Kuching.
swap.text: Name this dynasty that controlled the Miri oilfields and ruled Serawak from the mid-1800s to the mid-1900s.
swap.clue: The Japanese invasion of Borneo ended the rule of this dynasty, which began when the Sultan of Brunei rewarded the patriarch of this family with the Raj of Sarawak after crushing a tribal rebellion.
